summary: Greece runs competitive auctions with market-linked premiums, now also for grid-scale batteries, and corporate PPAs are growing fast. The market is open to foreign investors, but connection terms and curtailment are the main concerns for lenders.

access.reason: Law 4414/2016 set up auctions with market-linked premiums, a form of Contract for Difference, and recent auctions added battery storage support.

terms.reason: Premiums are paid against a reference price set in competitive tenders.

ownership.reason: There are no general restrictions on foreign investment in renewables, and funds can be converted and moved freely.

build.reason: Investors and lenders focus on connection terms and curtailment risk, though licensing was sped up in 2020.

stability.reason: A 2022 Climate Law sets emissions targets, and the target is 80% renewable electricity by 2030.

direction.reason: Storage auctions and fast-growing corporate PPAs widen the revenue options for projects.

access.reason: Industrial and corporate PPAs with utility-scale projects are growing rapidly.

ownership.reason: No general restrictions on foreign investment in renewables.

build.reason: Curtailment and connection terms are key risks.

stability.reason: Targets are set in law and no retroactive change was found.

direction.reason: Corporate PPA activity is growing rapidly.

events.title: Rising curtailment cuts renewable revenues and makes banks more cautious
National Climate Law sets a 55% emissions cut by 2030
